newsitem.title: UK: ICI hits 2-yr low as analysts cut forecasts.
newsitem.headline: ICI hits 2-yr low as analysts cut forecasts.

text.p: Shares in Imperial Chemical Industries Plc touched a two-year low on Monday as analysts lowered earnings estimates amid talk of continuing pricing pressures on the group.
ICI shares were down 16p at 686-1/2 by 1530 GMT in volume of 3.2 million shares, after earlier touching a low of 680p -- the lowest since March 1995.
At HSBC James Capel, analyst David Ingles lowered his 1997 pre-tax, pre-exceptional profit estimate to 600 million stg from 750 million and cut his 1998 forecast to 800 million stg from 900 million.
Ingles, who repeated a "sell" rating on ICI shares, also expects ICI to take a 100 million restructuring charge in both years.

At SBC Warburg analysts cut their current-year estimate to 565 million stg from 635 million while rating the stock a "buy," and at NatWest analysts said their forecasts "look vulnerable" and repeated a "hold" rating.
Dealers said the latest round of downgrades followed briefings with the company on trading in the first quarter.
Ingles said a hoped-for improvement in trading conditions during the first quarter of the year had not materialised.
Instead, pricing pressures continued in a range of basic materials such as PTA and PET -- used in making plastics -- and titanium dioxide, used to give whiteness to paint and paper products.

"Everyone knows they had a pretty awful start to the year and it's not going to get better overnight," said Ingles. "I do think prices are beginning to make progress but it's just not being shown yet in ICI's results."
"It should start to come through from the second quarter but progress is slow and it's not showing up as strongly as we had hoped," the Capel analyst said.
ICI shares have underperformed the All-Share index by 22 percent in the last six months and 34 percent over the past 12 month period.

However, Ingles said the disappointing performance by ICI should not necessarily reflect on the rest of the chemical sector. "A lot of the second line chemical shares are looking very good value," he said.
A spokesman for ICI declined comment on the latest downgrades.

He said any briefings for analysts would have been part of normal contacts with the company before the start of its "closed" season, when official comment is effectively barred in the run-up to results.
ICI reports first quarter results on April 24.
